facts: Tomahawk 6 is a 102.4 Tb/s switch family. Host retimers such as Astera PCIe/CXL products are distinct from optical-module DSPs.

parts.name: SerDes edge

roadmap.change: Scenario: optical engines beside the ASIC shorten the electrical path.
roadmap.tradeoff: Thermal design, package yield and serviceability become harder.

B2.status: Ara baseline: mass volume Mar 2026. Taurus: announced / showcased Mar 2026
B2.function: Conditions high-speed electrical signals for an optical link. Implementations can equalize, retime and adapt the link; this is not an application processor.
facts: Marvell Ara uses 3 nm technology and supports 1.6T at 200G per lane.
Ara T / Ara X were sampling from Q1 2026; do not equate them with baseline Ara volume status.
Broadcom introduced Taurus at 400G per lane. A lane rate is not the module aggregate rate.

parts.name: Electrical I/O / SerDes
parts.detail: Lane interfaces receive and transmit high-speed electrical signals.

parts.name: Conversion / analog front end
parts.detail: Illustrates the analog/digital interface; exact ADC/DAC partition is vendor-specific.

parts.name: Equalization / DSP logic
parts.detail: Processes a distorted signal to improve recoverability. This is a conceptual block, not a vendor floorplan.

parts.name: Package / power / thermal
parts.detail: Supplies power and routes I/O; heat and electrical parasitics constrain integration.

roadmap.title: Higher-rate lanes
roadmap.change: Current direction: 200G to 400G per lane. Analog bandwidth and digital equalization must support the higher rate. Future 3.2T requires an appropriate lane count and complete optical/electrical ecosystem.
roadmap.tradeoff: Fewer lanes can simplify routing, but noise margin, heat and signal integrity become harder. Exact future block specs are not in the filings.

roadmap.title: Selective retiming
roadmap.change: Ara T is a transmit-retimed design. LRO architectures retain transmit retiming and use a linear receive path; this changes DSP content rather than merely shrinking the package.
roadmap.tradeoff: Reduced processing can narrow interoperability or channel-loss margins. Architecture qualification matters.

filing.scope: Read filing evidence for business exposure and constraints; selected relevant filings, not a certified latest-filing index.

records.title: Marvell Q2 FY2027 Form 10-Q
records.claim: Marvell completed its acquisition of Celestial AI on February 2, 2026. The filing describes Celestial's Photonic Fabric as a next-generation scale-up interconnect platform and says the acquisition is expected to accelerate AI/cloud connectivity strategy.
records.limitation: An acquisition and its strategic rationale do not prove optical-I/O volume adoption or specify a future DSP floorplan.

records.title: Broadcom Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q
records.claim: Broadcom attributes semiconductor growth to custom AI accelerators and AI networking. Its risk discussion identifies lower power and higher bandwidth as technology requirements, while warning about unsupported competing technologies and customer-owned tooling.
records.limitation: The filing is business evidence, not proof of a particular CPO package, DSP process node, lane rate or power reduction. Precise product specifications need technical sources.

records.title: Coherent Q3 FY2026 Form 10-Q
records.claim: Coherent reports strong AI-datacenter transceiver demand and says it is expanding indium-phosphide capacity in Sherman, Texas, in response to customer demand and industry shortage. Its segment spans transceivers, modules, components, optics and semiconductor devices.
records.limitation: Capacity investment does not establish the share allocated to CPO, specific laser product yields, or guaranteed returns.

records.title: Lumentum Q3 FY2026 Form 10-Q
records.claim: Lumentum says cloud/AI demand is outpacing supply and it is investing in capacity internally and with contract manufacturers. It discloses components such as semiconductor laser chips and subsystems, and systems including optical modules and optical circuit switches.
records.limitation: It identifies clean-room capacity, staff, complex processes, equipment ramp and possible underutilization as constraints. Do not infer that every new capacity dollar is CPO-specific.

records.title: Applied Optoelectronics Q2 2026 Form 10-Q
records.claim: AAOI describes in-house laser/component and datacenter-transceiver production in Texas, transceiver production in Taiwan, and transceiver/subassembly plus CATV manufacturing in China. It performs laser and optical-module R&D.
records.limitation: This supports vertically integrated exposure; it does not establish a proprietary merchant DSP business or a filing-verified 3.2T product roadmap.

records.title: Fabrinet FY2026 Form 10-K
records.claim: Fabrinet's disclosed capabilities include optical/precision packaging, reliability testing, fiber alignment and complex PCB assembly. It manufactures for OEM customers, in some cases as the sole outsourced manufacturing partner, and emphasizes that it does not compete in their end markets.
records.limitation: Fabrinet is a manufacturing-service exposure, not necessarily the owner of an optical-module design. More complex packaging benefits it only if customers award programs and capacity is utilized.

records.title: AXT Q2 2026 Form 10-Q
records.claim: AXT says its three substrate families require Chinese export permits. It specifically calls InP permits its most significant challenge, with order backlog awaiting approval and unpredictable permit timing.
records.limitation: Demand for InP does not necessarily turn promptly into shipments or revenue; substrate opportunity must be separated from export access.

records.title: Corning Q2 2026 Form 10-Q
records.claim: Corning identifies fiber, cable and connectivity for datacenters and networks among its products. It attributes Optical Communications growth to strong demand for generative-AI products and discusses capacity/technology investment to support customers.
records.limitation: This supports fiber/connectivity exposure across architectures, but not a particular multicore-fiber capability or exact CPO revenue amount.

records.title: POET Q2 2026 MD&A furnished with Form 6-K
records.claim: POET describes optical-interposer integration of electronic and photonic devices, including TIAs and laser drivers, to improve performance and lower module-assembly cost. It discusses optical engines for pluggables and external light-source products for emerging architectures.
records.limitation: Management's claimed advantages are not independent performance validation. Product qualification can fail or take longer than expected; a design win is a sales opportunity, not guaranteed recurring production.

records.title: NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Form 10-Q
records.claim: NVIDIA's Compute & Networking segment includes datacenter computing and networking platforms. Its cost disclosures explicitly include fabrication, assembly, testing, packaging and final-test yield fallout; revenue is concentrated among relatively few direct and indirect customers.
records.limitation: The filing alone does not specify Spectrum-X Photonics optical-engine geometry, prove CPO eliminates all DSPs, or quantify the revenue of any packaging supplier.

records.title: Amkor FY2025 Form 10-K
records.claim: Amkor explicitly reports co-development of silicon photonics and co-packaged optics. Its capabilities include high-density fan-out, 2.5D integration, advanced flip chip, fine-pitch bumping, wafer-level processing and advanced system-in-package.
records.limitation: The same filing emphasizes capital intensity, cyclicality and utilization. CPO collaboration does not mean every CPO program is awarded to Amkor or that optical revenue is separately measurable.

records.title: ASE Technology Q1 2026 results furnished on Form 6-K
records.claim: ASE identifies its services as packaging, front-end engineering test, wafer probing, final test and electronic manufacturing services. It discloses substantial customer concentration in both assembly/test and EMS.
records.limitation: This filing verifies general packaging/test exposure. It does not establish a specific CPO design win or CPO share of revenue; not the latest available quarter and not represented as such.

records.title: Teradyne Q1 2026 Form 10-Q
records.claim: Teradyne discloses its May 2025 acquisition of Quantifi Photonics, describing it as a PIC-test provider whose acquisition enables scalable PIC testing. Quantifi is included in Product Test.
records.limitation: Standalone Quantifi revenue was not disclosed because the financial impact was not material. Testing opportunity should not be equated with a large existing optical earnings contribution; this is an earlier quarter.

records.title: Coherent Q3 FY2026 Form 10-Q: manufacturing economics
records.claim: Coherent attributes gross-margin improvement partly to lower input costs, shorter production cycle times and improved yields in Datacenter & Communications.
records.limitation: Yield and cycle-time improvements can create value without a new nominal line rate. The filing does not disclose die-level yield targets or attribute all margin change to one technology.

records.title: POET Q2 2026 MD&A: commercialization constraint
records.claim: POET describes customer qualification through product sampling, reliability testing and engineering collaboration, and acknowledges limited operating history in the datacenter market.
records.limitation: A future-product visualization must distinguish sampled, qualified and shipping products; a product list is not evidence of broad volume adoption.

scenarios.title: If DSP-based 1.6T/3.2T pluggables remain important
scenarios.conclusion: Merchant DSP suppliers such as Marvell and Broadcom retain opportunity, together with lasers, drivers/TIAs and transceiver assembly. Lane-rate/product evidence must come from technical documentation; filings support exposure and commercialization risks, not precise future block specifications.

scenarios.title: If selected links adopt LPO or CPO
scenarios.conclusion: Standalone module-DSP content and conventional pluggable assembly can face substitution on those links. Treat Marvell/Broadcom and AAOI/Fabrinet as businesses needing architecture/mix analysis, not automatic companies to avoid: diversified exposure and growing aggregate optical demand can offset displacement.

scenarios.title: If optical engines move closer to host silicon
scenarios.conclusion: Attention shifts to heterogeneous integration, short electrical interconnects, fiber attach, thermal management and known-good-die testing. Amkor has explicit filing-disclosed CPO collaboration; ASE and Fabrinet have relevant capabilities but require program-specific proof. Packaging complexity alone does not guarantee any supplier's revenue.

scenarios.title: If silicon-photonics and external-light-source adoption grows
scenarios.conclusion: Coherent and Lumentum merit attention for optical components and capacity; POET offers interposer/light-source development exposure with higher qualification uncertainty. AXT's material opportunity is constrained by export approvals, so demand strength alone is insufficient.

scenarios.title: If package complexity and optical port counts rise
scenarios.conclusion: PIC test and fiber connectivity are relevant enabling functions. Teradyne has filing-confirmed PIC-test capability through Quantifi, and Corning has fiber/connectivity exposure. Do not describe all testing or packaging spending as optical revenue or infer purchase contracts from industry position.
